This Islamic call to prayer, traditionally recited by a muezzin from a mosque's minaret, summons Muslims to each of the five daily obligatory prayers. What is it?
Adhan is the Islamic call to prayer, usually recited by a muezzin, traditionally from the minaret of a mosque, shortly before each of the five obligatory daily prayers.

Bloody Mary (folklore) is a legend of a ghost, phantom, witch, or spirit conjured to reveal the future.
Offspring of the monsters Echidna and Typhon, this three-headed hound with a serpent's tail guards the gates of the underworld — which mythological creature?
Cerberus (or; Ancient), often referred to as the hound of Hades, is a multi-headed dog that guards the gates of the underworld to prevent the dead from leaving.

This economic and cultural phenomenon holds that shoppers' free choices should drive what manufacturers produce, shaping a society built around acquiring more than what's strictly needed — which term?

Consumerism is a socio-cultural and economic phenomenon in which the aspirations of many individuals include the acquisition of goods and services beyond those necessary for survival or traditional displays.
Having followed his political patron from Shanghai to Beijing, this official now ranks first among China's vice premiers and sixth on the Communist Party's Politburo Standing Committee — who is he?

Born Gülbaran in 1955, this woman currently serves as the first lady of Turkey, married to the nation's president — who is she?
Emine Erdoğan (ne Glbaran; born 16 February 1955) is the current first lady of Turkey as the wife of President Recep Tayyip Erdoan.
As Italy's interior minister he restructured the police and secret services, then rose to become the country's president from 1985 to 1992 - who was he?
Francesco Cossiga (26 July 1928 - 17 August 2010) was an Italian politician who served as the president of Italy from 1985 to 1992.
At age 36, this mayor-turned-politician's vice-presidential run alongside Prabowo Subianto proved controversial, given he's the eldest child of Indonesia's seventh president — who is he?

Credited with introducing the words 'manpower' and 'heartland' into English, this British geographer was a founding father of geopolitics and the first director of the LSE — who was he?
Halford Mackinder (15 February 1861 - 6 March 1947) was a British geographer, academic and politician, who is regarded as one of the founding fathers of both geopolitics and geostrategy.

This mythological Greek hero led a legendary crew in search of a Golden Fleece, and later married the sorceress Medea, granddaughter of the sun god — who was he?
Jason (Ancient) was an ancient Greek mythological hero and leader of the Argonauts, whose quest for the Golden Fleece is featured in Greek literature.
As military governor of Paris in 1914, this French officer helped win the First Battle of the Marne — famously rushing troops to the front in commandeered taxicabs. Who was he?

Joseph Gallieni (24 April 1849 - 27 May 1916) was a French military officer, active for most of his career as a military commander and administrator in the French colonies where he wrote several books on colonial affairs.
Its guiding symbol is the Six Arrows, and it centers on secularism, gender equality, and economic statism as introduced by modern Turkey's first president — which ideology is it?

A Harvard law professor who founded Creative Commons, this legal scholar briefly ran for the Democratic presidential nomination in 2016 before dropping out ahead of the primaries. Who is he?
Lawrence Lessig (born June 3, 1961) is an American legal scholar and political activist.
Born in Atar and trained at French military school, this officer fought against the Polisario Front before taking power in a bloodless coup and ruling Mauritania from 1984 to 2005 — who was he?
Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya (born 28 November 1941) is a Mauritanian military officer and politician who served as the President of Mauritania from 1984 to 2005.
Born in north Belfast, this Ulster-born lawyer became Ireland's second female president — and the first woman anywhere to directly succeed another woman in the office. Who was she?
Mary McAleese (ne Leneghan; born 27 June 1951) is an Irish activist lawyer, academic, author, and former politician who served as the president of Ireland from November 1997 to November 2011.
A 1991 graduate of an elite airborne academy, this Ukrainian-born officer has led Russia's paratrooper forces since 2022 - who is he?
Mikhail Teplinsky (born 9 January 1969) is a Ukrainian-born Russian military officer who has served as commander of the Russian Airborne Forces since 2022.
He commanded Bosnian government forces defending the surrounded Srebrenica enclave during the Bosnian War, and was later tried at The Hague over the treatment of detainees — which officer was he?

Naser Orić (born 3 March 1967) is a Bosnian former officer who commanded Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina (ARBiH) forces in the Srebrenica enclave in eastern Bosnia surrounded by Bosnian Serb forces, during the Bosnian War.
This legendary king of Ithaca, husband of Penelope and father of Telemachus, is renowned for his cunning intellect and is the hero of one of Homer's two great epic poems — who is he?
Odysseus (Ancient), also known by the Latin variant Ulysses (UK also), is a legendary Greek king of Ithaca and the hero of Homer's epic poem, the Odyssey.
A Spanish politician and economist who has served as Prime Minister of Spain since 2018 and as Secretary-General of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party. Who is he?
Pedro Sánchez (born 29 February 1972) is a Spanish politician and economist who has served as Prime Minister of Spain since 2018.
In Catholic theology, this is a passing intermediate state after death for purifying a soul before it enters Heaven, often likened to dross being burned from gold in a furnace. What is it?
Purgatory is a belief in Catholic theology. Purgatory (Latin: purgatorium, borrowed into English via Anglo-Norman and Old French) is a belief in Catholic theology.
Hailed as the "chief founder of England's naval supremacy," this Cromwell-era general at sea had his fame deliberately expunged after the Stuart Restoration — who was he?
Robert Blake (admiral) (27 September 1598 - 7 August 1657) was an English naval officer who served as general at sea and the Lord Warden of the Cinque Ports from 1656 to 1657.

An American Founding Father and statesman (1722–1803), signatory of the Declaration of Independence, and second cousin to another Founding Father of the same surname. A leader in the movement for American independence. Who is this?
Samuel Adams was Founding Father of the United States (1722–1803).

Nicknamed for both his towering height and a 23-year run as head of government, this Swedish statesman was a chief architect of the "Swedish Model" welfare state — who was he?
Tage Erlander (13 June 1901 - 21 June 1985) was a Swedish politician and statesman who served as Prime Minister of Sweden and leader of the Social Democratic Party from 1946 to 1969.
This Indian politician, the son of a Tamil Nadu chief minister, served as the state's youngest-ever deputy chief minister before becoming Opposition Leader in 2026. Who is he?

A leading German industrialist who organized the Reich's wartime raw-materials effort, this Weimar foreign minister was assassinated in 1922, just months into the post. Who was he?

Hinduism: Range of Indian religious traditions. Vaidika Dharma (lit. 'Vedic dharma') and Arya Dharma are historical endonyms for Hinduism.

Lady of the Lake: Sorceress in Arthurian legend. As either single character or multiple ones, the figure of the Lady of the Lake often appears in various roles in the works of modern culture.

Libertarianism: Political philosophy based on liberty. Different categorizations have been used to distinguish these various forms of libertarianism.

First flown in 1987, this medium-lift helicopter began as a joint UK-Italian venture between Westland and Agusta, and several countries use the nickname 'Merlin' for it — which helicopter is it?
AgustaWestland AW101 is a medium-lift helicopter in military and civil use.
With a wingspan up to 3.3 meters and a weight of 15 kilograms, which South American bird is generally considered the largest bird of prey on Earth, sporting a ruff of white feathers around its neck?
Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
This amino acid carries a guanidino group that serves as the body's precursor for making nitric oxide, and it's encoded by a generous six codons. Which one is it?
Arginine is the amino acid with the formula (H2N)(HN)CN(H)(CH2)3CH(NH2)CO2H.
Only eight species of this stocky-legged, shaggy, short-tailed carnivoran survive, ranging across North and South America and Eurasia — what mammal is it?
Bear are carnivoran mammals of the family Ursidae.

This general medical term describes blood escaping a damaged vessel, whether internally or through a puncture in the skin, with the loss of more than about 15 percent of total volume proving potentially fatal. What is it called?
Bleeding is blood escaping from the circulatory system from damaged blood vessels.

This British dog breed of mastiff type has a stocky build, a large head, thick facial skin folds, and a protruding lower jaw, and is now illegal to breed in the Netherlands over health concerns — name the breed?
Bulldog is a British breed of dog of mastiff type. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.

This quaternary ammonium compound ferries long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for energy production, and is concentrated in heart and skeletal muscle, though most people synthesize enough on their own. What is it called?
Carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound involved in metabolism in most mammals, plants, and some bacteria.
Present naturally in breast milk and added to infant formula, this essential nutrient is also a building block for a neurotransmitter that controls muscle movement — which compound?
Choline is a cation with the chemical formula +.
Named for its snake-like neck (its species epithet means 'snake'), this feisty freshwater reptile has powerful beak-like jaws and ranges from Nova Scotia down to Florida — which species is it?
Common snapping turtle (Chelydra serpentina) is a species of large, freshwater turtles in the family Chelydridae.

This closed sac within the body has a distinct wall of cells that are structurally abnormal compared to surrounding tissue, and may contain air, fluid, or semi-solid material — unlike a pus-filled abscess, what is it called?
Cyst is a closed sac in the body, having a distinct envelope and division compared with the nearby tissue.

Derived from the wild rock dove and split into more than 350 distinct breeds, this domesticated bird was already being bred by Mesopotamians more than 5,000 years ago, according to cuneiform tablets — what's the bird?
Domestic pigeon (Columba livia "domestica" or Columba livia forma domestica) is a domesticated bird derived from the rock dove (Columba livia), of which it is also a subspecies.
Psychology, medicine, history, and even computer science all study these pleasure-or-displeasure states, which still lack any agreed scientific definition — what are they?
Emotion are physical and mental states brought on by neurophysiological changes, variously associated with thoughts, feelings, behavioral responses, and a degree of pleasure or displeasure.
Equivalent to one coulomb per volt, this SI unit of electrical capacitance is named after a pioneering English physicist — name the unit?
Farad (symbol: F) is the unit of electrical capacitance, the ability of a body to store an electrical charge, in the International System of Units (SI), equivalent to 1 coulomb per volt (C/V).
Alongside co-founding a file-sharing site, this Swedish entrepreneur also started an internet service provider and web-hosting firm called PRQ — who is he?
Fredrik Neij (born 27 April 1978), alias TiAMO, is the co-founder of The Pirate Bay, and the Swedish Internet service provider and web hosting company PRQ.

Designed at a major tech company in 2007 by Robert Griesemer, Rob Pike, and Ken Thompson, this statically typed, compiled programming language borrows C-like syntax while adding garbage collection and built-in concurrency support — name the language?
Go (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose programming language that is statically typed and compiled.

A spiny mammal with 17 species across five genera in Europe, Asia, and Africa, this creature shares distant ancestry with shrews. There are no native populations in Australia or the Americas, though one extinct genus once roamed North America—what is it?
Hedgehog is a spiny mammal of the subfamily Erinaceinae, in the eulipotyphlan family Erinaceidae.
Petroleum, natural gas, and coal all fall under which class of organic compound built solely from hydrogen and carbon, spanning gases, liquids, waxes, and polymers?
Hydrocarbon is an organic compound consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon.

This analytical framework, which arose partly in reaction to both white feminism and the male-dominated Black liberation movement, examines how overlapping social identities create unique combinations of discrimination and privilege — name the concept?
Intersectionality is an analytical framework for understanding how groups' and individuals' social and political identities result in unique combinations of discrimination and privilege.
Court astronomer and advisor to Elizabeth I, this mathematician and alchemist kept one of England's largest libraries and is credited with coining the phrase 'British Empire' — who was he?
John Dee (13 July 1527 - December 1608 or March 1609) was an English mathematician, astronomer, teacher, astrologer, occultist, and alchemist.
Named from the Greek word for 'the hidden one', this colorless, odorless noble gas with atomic number 36 is used in fluorescent lamps and high-powered gas lasers. Name the element?
Krypton (from Ancient) is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

This Finnish-American software engineer has led development of a hugely popular open-source operating system kernel since 1991, and also created the distributed version-control system Git — who is he?
Linus Torvalds (born 28 December 1969) is a Finnish and American software engineer who is the creator and lead developer of the Linux kernel since 1991.
This naturally occurring white solid, found as the mineral brucite, has very low water solubility and is a key ingredient in a well-known antacid remedy — what is it?
Magnesium hydroxide is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula Mg(OH)2.
Shaped like a half-moon, this crescent of fibrocartilage partly divides the knee joint and also turns up in the wrist, jaw, and shoulder joints — what is it called?
Meniscus (anatomy) (pl.: menisci or meniscuses) is a crescent-shaped fibrocartilaginous anatomical structure that, in contrast to an articular disc, only partly divides a joint cavity.
Named from a Greek word for lead because its ores were once confused with lead ore, this chemical element bears the symbol Mo and atomic number 42 — name the element?
Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.
A naval aviator who flew the F9F Panther in Korea before commanding Apollo 11, this Ohio-born engineer earned a place in history in 1969 — who is he?
Neil Armstrong (August 5, 1930 - August 25, 2012) was an American astronaut and aeronautical engineer who, as the commander of the 1969 Apollo 11 mission, became the first person to walk on the Moon.
Many species in this bird family scavenge alongside pigeons and gulls, while two of its city-dwelling members are famous for nesting directly on buildings — which family are they?
Old World sparrow are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Believed to have originated in Sardinia and cultivated since around the 3rd century BC, this flowering herb native to Greece and North Africa is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Parsley (Petroselinum crispum), is a species of flowering plant in the family Apiaceae that is native to Greece, the Balkans, Algeria and Morocco.

Left untreated, this inherited metabolic disorder — caused by a faulty gene needed to break down a certain amino acid — can cause intellectual disability, seizures, and a musty body odor — what is it?
Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inborn error of metabolism that results in decreased metabolism of the amino acid phenylalanine.
This category of polymer includes both natural proteins like wool and silk, and synthetic materials like nylon and aramid fibers — what is it?
Polyamide is a polymer with repeating units linked by amide bonds.

Harvested from the seeds of several Plantago species, this common dietary fiber supplement relieves both constipation and mild diarrhea, and occasionally doubles as a food thickener — what is it called?
Psyllium is the common name used for several members of the plant genus Plantago whose seeds are used commercially for the production of mucilage.
Derived from an Ancient Greek word for 'flow,' this umbrella term covers more than 200 different conditions causing chronic joint or connective-tissue pain, including arthritis — what's the term?
Rheumatism (from the Ancient Greek, rhema) or rheumatic disorders are conditions causing chronic, often intermittent pain affecting the joints or connective tissue.
Which genus of 20 to 30 species of flowering plants in the family Adoxaceae produces both a fragrant white flower cluster and a dark berry, each with their own distinct common name?

Sambucus is a genus of between 20 and 30 species of flowering plants in the family Adoxaceae. The various species are commonly referred to as elder, with the flowers as elderflower, and the fruit as elderberry.
Believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso, this toy dog breed originated in Tibet — name the breed?
Shih Tzu is a toy dog or pet dog breed originating from Tibet and believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso.

This now-discredited scientific theory held that living creatures like fleas or maggots could regularly arise directly from non-living matter such as dust or rotting flesh, and was coherently synthesized by Aristotle. Name the theory?
Spontaneous generation is a superseded scientific theory that held that living creatures could arise from non-living matter and that such processes were commonplace and regular.
Down, Wolf–Hirschhorn, and Andersen–Tawil are all named examples of this medical term for a cluster of correlated signs and symptoms — what is it?
Syndrome is a set of medical signs and symptoms which are correlated with each other and often associated with a particular disease or disorder.
Known in medical Latin as the pollex, this digit sits outermost on the hand when you stand palms-forward — which body part?
Thumb is the first digit of the hand, next to the index finger.
Developed by Microsoft as open-source software, this programming language adds optional static typing to JavaScript and transpiles back into it — name the language?
TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.
Named after the Scottish engineer who improved the Newcomen steam engine in 1776, this SI unit of power equals one joule per second — what is it?
Watt (symbol: W) is the unit of power or radiant flux in the International System of Units (SI), equal to 1 joule per second or 1 kgm2s3.
Discovered in 1849 and named for the Greek goddess of health, this nearly spherical body is the fourth-largest object in the main asteroid belt — which asteroid is it?
10 Hygiea: Fourth-largest asteroid. 10 Hygiea is a large asteroid in the outer region of the main asteroid belt, between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.

Nicknamed 'goutweed' and 'bishop's weed,' this shade-loving carrot-family plant is the type species of its genus and was introduced worldwide as an ornamental, becoming invasive — what is its scientific name?
Aegopodium podagraria: Species of flowering plant in the celery family.
Named for its carbon-carbon double bond, this class of hydrocarbon includes terminal versions known as alpha-olefins — what's the general term for it?
Alkene: Hydrocarbon compound containing one or more C=C bonds.
Also called water boas, these semiaquatic South American snakes include the world's largest species by weight, a green-hued giant — which snakes?
Anaconda: Genus of snakes. Two to four extant and one extinct species are currently recognized, including one of the largest snakes in the world, E. murinus, the green anaconda.
When an injury to the wall of the body's main artery lets blood force its layers apart, victims often feel a sudden 'tearing' chest or back pain — what's this medical emergency called?
Aortic dissection: Injury to the innermost layer of the aorta.

With the symbol At and atomic number 85, this is the rarest naturally occurring element in Earth's crust, so radioactive that a macroscopic sample would instantly vaporize itself — what element is it?
Astatine: Chemical element with atomic number 85 (At). It is the rarest naturally occurring element in the Earth's crust, occurring only as the decay product of various heavier elements.

Once the go-to sedatives and anticonvulsants, these barbituric-acid-derived depressants were largely replaced by benzodiazepines and 'Z-drugs' because of their high addiction and overdose risk — what class of drugs?
Barbiturate: Class of depressant drugs derived from barbituric acid.
This English musician played bass on the Rolling Stones' first nineteen studio albums across three decades before later fronting his own blues outfit, the Rhythm Kings — who is he?
Developed alongside the 707 airliner from the same prototype, this narrower, shorter jet became the U.S. Air Force's first jet-powered refueling tanker in 1957 — name the aircraft?
Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker: US military aerial refueling and transport aircraft.
Sold under the brand name Pulmicort, this steroid drug treats asthma when inhaled but also comes as a nasal spray for allergies and a rectal foam for bowel disease — which medication?
This highly contagious virus, spread through feces, can kill up to 91% of untreated dogs and wolves and also strikes foxes, cats, and skunks — what is it?
Canine parvovirus: Contagious virus mainly affecting dogs.
Named for barbels that resemble a cat's whiskers, these scaleless, ray-finned fish include giants like the Mekong species and go by nicknames such as 'mud cat' in the Southern US — what are they?
Catfish: Order of fish. Catfish are a diverse group of ray-finned fish of the order Siluriformes (historically Nematognathi).
Domesticated from the red junglefowl roughly 8,000 years ago, this bird now numbers over 26 billion worldwide, more than any other domesticated species — what is it?
Chicken: Domesticated subspecies of red junglefowl. The chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.
Sold under the brand name Anafranil, this tricyclic antidepressant treats obsessive-compulsive disorder but also premature ejaculation and the cataplexy that comes with narcolepsy — which drug?
Clomipramine: Antidepressant. It has also been notably used to treat premature ejaculation and the cataplexy associated with narcolepsy.
The heaviest songbird on Earth and the most widely distributed of all the corvids, this all-black passerine averages 25 inches long across the Northern Hemisphere — what is it?
Common raven: Large, black species of passerine bird.

This academic framework examines how systemic bias against certain ethnic groups is embedded in laws and institutions, using the concept of intersectionality to explain overlapping forms of inequality — what is it called?
Critical race theory: Conceptual framework. The word critical in the name is an academic reference to critical theory, not criticizing or blaming individuals.

Dubbed the 'father of modern experimental optics,' this Scottish inventor discovered the angle and the photoelasticity that bear on polarized light — and improved the stereoscope along the way. Who was he?
David Brewster: British astronomer and mathematician (1781–1868)
Sold as Benadryl, this first-generation H1-antihistamine is famously sedating — yet at higher doses it can paradoxically cause agitation and restlessness instead of sleep; what's the drug?
Diphenhydramine: Antihistamine medication. Diphenhydramine, sold under the brand name Benadryl among others, is an antihistamine and sedative.
Known medically as cerumen, this waxy secretion in the ear canal protects against bacteria, fungi, and water while trapping dust and dead skin — what is it?
Earwax: Waxy substance secreted by the ear.

Distinguished by its massive head, huge size, and trademark black facial mask, this gentle British dog breed is now classed as vulnerable in its homeland, with just 104 UK births recorded in 2020 — which breed?
English Mastiff: British breed of dog. The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.
This small European finch's male sports a blue-grey cap and rust-red underparts, while both sexes flash white wing bars — what species is it?
Eurasian chaffinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs) is a common and widespread small passerine bird – in the finch family.
A feathery, yellow-flowered Mediterranean herb in the carrot family, this anise-tasting plant is one of the primary ingredients in absinthe — what is it?
Fennel: Flowering plant species in the carrot family.
Named for the mathematician who used it to solve the heat equation, this expansion writes a periodic function as an infinite sum of sines and cosines — what is it?
Fourier series: Decomposition of periodic functions.
Commonly known as snails and slugs, this class is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after insects — what is it called?
Gastropod: Class of molluscs. The fossil record of gastropods extends back to the Late Cambrian.
Occurring in the cytosol, this ten-step metabolic pathway breaks glucose down into pyruvate while generating ATP and NADH — what process is it?
Glycolysis: Series of interconnected biochemical reactions.

Once nearly all lumped into a single genus before 21st-century research proved that grouping polyphyletic, these grey-and-white seabirds have an older dialect name, 'mew,' echoing their calls — which birds?
Gull: Subfamily of seabirds. The large species take up to four years to attain full adult plumage, but two years is typical for small gulls.
Comprising cicadas, aphids, bed bugs, and more than 80,000 other species with piercing-sucking mouthparts, which insect order is nicknamed the 'true bugs'?
Hemiptera: Order of insects often called true bugs.
Often called the founder of alpinism and modern meteorology, this Genevan scientist is also credited with building the first successful solar oven — who was he?
Horace Bénédict de Saussure: Genevan scientist and mountaineer (1740–1799)
Marked in its severe stage by hallucinations and paradoxical undressing, which condition is defined as a body core temperature below 35 degrees Celsius?
Hypothermia: Human body core temperature below 35 °C (95 °F)
This ring-shaped structure in the eye controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the size of the pupil — and it's also what determines eye color — what is it?
Iris (anatomy): Colored part of an eye.
Son of Taiwanese immigrants, this engineer launched the world's most valuable company from a Denny's restaurant in 1993 after earning a Stanford master's degree — who is he?
Jensen Huang: Taiwanese and American businessman (born 1963)
Nicknamed the 'miracle leaf' and 'life plant,' this Madagascar-native succulent sprouts tiny new plantlets right along the edges of its leaves — which species?

Kalanchoe pinnata: Succulent plant native to Madagascar. Kalanchoe pinnata, commonly known as cathedral bells, air plant, life plant, miracle leaf, and love bush, is a succulent plant native to Madagascar.

Native to the tropical Americas, this flowering shrub was carried to Europe by Dutch explorers and later brought to Goa by the Portuguese, becoming a notorious invasive weed across some 50 countries — which plant?
Lantana camara: Species of plant. Lantana camara (common lantana) is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family (Verbenaceae), native to the tropics of the Americas.
Named after the Italian word for lemon, this citrus-scented compound comes in two mirror-image forms — one smelling of oranges, the other like pine — what is it?

Born into one of Europe's richest families in Vienna, this philosopher studied under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge before giving away his inheritance and enlisting in the Austro-Hungarian Army — who is he?
Ludwig Wittgenstein: Austrian philosopher and logician (1889–1951)

First isolated in the 1770s and carrying atomic number 25, this hard, silvery transition metal is a key alloying agent in stainless steel and also an essential trace nutrient in the human diet — which element?
Manganese: Chemical element with atomic number 25 (Mn)

Co-inventor of a heart-valve repair device called the MitraClip, this Turkish-American cardiac surgeon became a famous TV health personality before being named the 17th administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services in 2025 — who is he?
Mehmet Oz: American TV host and government official (born 1960)
Sitting atop the brainstem and linking it to the diencephalon and cerebrum, this structure governs vision, hearing, motor control, and arousal -- what is it called?
Midbrain: Forward-most portion of the brainstem.
Native to tropical Central and South America, this genus of 59 flowering plant species belongs to the arum family — which genus?
NASA was formed in 1958 by absorbing which older federal aeronautics body?
The National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics had run American aeronautical research since 1915. The Space Race turned it into a space agency.
Present in 26 African countries with one of its largest undisturbed populations at Kenya's Lake Turkana, which large crocodilian sees adult males reach 3.5 to 5 metres long?
This British engineer rewrote Maxwell's equations into the form we use today and devised the telegrapher's equations — who was he?
Oliver Heaviside: British mathematician and electrical engineer (1850–1925)
Discovered in 1802 and named after a newly found asteroid, this silvery-white platinum-group metal is prized for cleaning up automobile exhaust in catalytic converters — which element?
Palladium: Chemical element with atomic number 46 (Pd)

Famous for the giant throat pouch beneath its long beak, this large water bird's eight living species range from the tropics to temperate zones, with some even flying inland to Australia's Red Centre after heavy rains — what bird is this?
Pelican: Genus of large water birds with a throat pouch.
With a phosphate-charged head and two fatty-acid tails joined by glycerol, this molecule builds neuron membranes and can decline up to 20% by age 80 — what is it?
Sitting less than a degree from the north celestial pole, this yellow supergiant is famously steady for navigation — but is secretly a triple star system. What is it?
Polaris: Northern pole-star; brightest star in Ursa Minor.

Diagnosed in about 8% of male urology visits in the US, this umbrella term covers several bacterial and non-bacterial pelvic conditions, despite its name not always involving actual inflammation — which condition?
Prostatitis: Medical condition. Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.
Named partly for Jack Northrop, designer of a tailless aircraft, which genus of enormous azhdarchid pterosaur is a top candidate for the largest flying animal ever?
Quetzalcoatlus: Genus of azhdarchid pterosaurs from the Late Cretaceous.

Marked by tea-colored urine and triggered by crush injuries or extreme exertion, this condition involves skeletal muscle breaking down so fast that released myoglobin can damage the kidneys — what is it called?
Rhabdomyolysis: Condition in which damaged skeletal muscle breaks down rapidly.
This German engineer invented a fuel-efficient combustion engine so influential that both it and the fuel it burns bear his name — who was he?
Rudolf Diesel: German inventor and engineer (1858–1913)
Typically emerging in young adulthood with hallucinations and delusions, this disorder has no objective lab test and needs symptoms for at least six months under the DSM-5 — what is it?
Schizophrenia: Mental disorder with psychotic symptoms.
Nicknamed the 'brushwood dog' for its game-flushing hunting style, this is the smallest of Japan's six native dog breeds — which breed?
Shiba Inu: Japanese dog breed. The Shiba Inu (Japanese: 柴犬; Japanese pronunciation: [ɕi.ba.i.nɯ]) is a breed of hunting dog from Japan.
First isolated in 1820 from black nightshade berries, this glycoalkaloid poison also occurs naturally in potatoes as a built-in pest defense. What compound is it?
Solanine: Glycoalkaloid poison found in the nightshade family of plants.
For 30 years this English theoretical astrophysicist held Cambridge's most prestigious academic post—the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics. Who?
Native to tropical Africa, this berry's glycoprotein — called miraculin — tricks your tongue into tasting sour foods like lemons and limes as sweet; what is this plant commonly nicknamed?
Synsepalum dulcificum: Plant from West Africa with a taste-modifying berry.

This congenital heart defect combines four distinct abnormalities — including a hole between the ventricles and a narrowed pulmonary exit — and can trigger cyanotic 'spells' in infants — what is this condition?
Tetralogy of Fallot: Type of congenital heart defect. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), formerly known as Steno-Fallot tetralogy, is a congenital heart defect characterized by four specific cardiac defects.
This white compound found in sunscreen, paint, and food coloring under the number E171 makes up two-thirds of all pigments used worldwide and is valued at over $13 billion — what is it?
Titanium dioxide: Chemical compound. Titanium dioxide, also known as titanium(IV) oxide or titania, is the inorganic compound derived from titanium with the chemical formula TiO2.
Nicknamed 'Crusty' by NATO, this twin-engined Soviet airliner featured a glazed nose and could operate from unpaved airfields — which aircraft is it?
Described from Mongolian fossils in 1924 and smaller than relatives like Deinonychus, which feathered, sickle-clawed dinosaur genus roamed Late Cretaceous Asia?
Velociraptor: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur. The type species is V. mongoliensis, named and described in 1924.
A slow-moving filter-feeder and the largest known fish alive — the biggest reliably recorded stretched nearly 19 metres — this is the only living member of its family. What is it?
Whale shark: Largest living species of fish. The whale shark (Rhincodon typus) is a slow-moving, filter-feeding carpet shark and the largest known extant fish species.
These striped African equines share their genus with horses and asses, and the leading theory says their patterns evolved mainly to deter biting flies — what are they?
Zebra: Striped animal in the equid family.
What is the chemical symbol for bohrium?
The symbol for bohrium is Bh. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.

Batman Begins is a 2005 superhero film based on the DC Comics character Batman.

Million Dollar Baby is a 2004 American sports drama film directed, co-produced, scored by and starring Clint Eastwood from a screenplay by Paul Haggis.
